input.question: Why do scars heal but leave a mark?
input.ground_truth: The skin you were born with took months to carefully grow in a controlled environment. When it gets badly damaged, your body doesn't have the time or conditions to replace it with identical tissue, so it rushes out a job to seal the wound, leaving out stuff like hair follicles and sweat glands to get the job done quicker.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do scars heal but leave a mark?

Answer:

response.prediction: When you get a cut or hurt your skin, your body sends special helpers called cells to fix it. These cells work hard to close the cut and make new skin. But sometimes, the new skin looks a little different from the old skin. That’s why you can see a mark or a scar left behind. It’s like when you fix a torn piece of paper with tape—the paper is all together again, but you can still see where it was torn. That’s why scars stay, even after you heal!
